items.q: How long does a website take?
items.a: A marketing site typically goes from kickoff to live in 2 to 3 weeks. Larger sites with custom integrations or multilingual content can take 4 to 6 weeks. Either way, you get a fixed launch date in writing before the project starts.

items.q: Do you work with Polish companies? Do you speak Polish?
items.a: Yes. We work with Polish clients regularly: conversational Polish, fluent English, native Russian and Ukrainian. Contracts can be signed under Polish law and invoicing is handled with VAT EU.

items.q: Can you build a site in Ukrainian for the diaspora market?
items.a: Yes. Several of our projects ship in PL / EN / UA / RU simultaneously. We handle proper i18n routing, hreflang, locale-specific SEO and translation review with native speakers.

items.q: What happens after the project is delivered?
items.a: You get 30 days of bug-fix support included. After that, edits are billed at €50 per hour with a one-hour minimum. There is no forced monthly retainer — you only pay when you actually need work done.

items.q: How much does an AI chatbot or agent cost?
items.a: AI agents start at €1,500 for a focused use case (a FAQ assistant, a lead qualifier, a single-tool automation). A sales agent with CRM is from €2,500; a multi-tool agent with integrations runs €4,500–12,000. Final price after a 30-minute scoping call.

items.q: Do you build for Android as well as iOS?
items.a: Yes - cross-platform from a single codebase using React Native and Expo, then submitted to both the App Store and Google Play. If a project genuinely needs platform-native code, we say so upfront and quote it separately.

items.q: How is working with you different from hiring an agency?
items.a: You message the developer directly. No account managers, no junior developers handling your project while a senior signs off. The person you brief is the person writing the code. Decisions take minutes, not weeks.

items.q: Can you build a website that actually ranks on Google?
items.a: Yes — that's the default, not an upsell. Every site I build ships with technical SEO, schema markup, hreflang for multilingual pages, optimized Core Web Vitals and IndexNow pings on deploy. Most pages index within hours and start ranking within weeks.

items.q: Do you sign contracts?
items.a: Always. Every project starts with a written agreement covering scope, payment schedule, IP transfer, deadlines and what happens if either side wants out. Contracts can be in English or Polish.

items.q: What if I need changes after launch?
items.a: Edits are billed at €50 per hour, with a one-hour minimum. No forced monthly retainer. You can come back six months later with a small change and we'll handle it - same terms, same rate.

items.q: Do you work remotely? Where are your clients based?
items.a: Everything runs remotely, with clients across the EU, the UK, the US and beyond. Calls, demos and handover happen online; the contract and payment are remote too. Time zones are not an issue: I sync to your working hours.

items.q: What drives the price of a website?
items.a: The number of pages, the features, and whether you already have the content. A landing page is a different league than a shop with integrations. You get one fixed quote before we start — no hourly add-ons, no hidden costs along the way.

items.q: How long will it take?
items.a: A marketing site — 2–3 weeks from kickoff. A larger project with integrations and multiple languages — 4–6 weeks. The date is fixed in writing before we start.

items.q: What do you need from me to get going?
items.a: Ideally your copy, photos and logo. Don't have them? I'll help put them together — just tell me about the business and I'll lead you through the rest. I won't sit waiting months for materials.

items.q: Will the site be optimized for Google (SEO)?
items.a: Yes. Every site ships with technical SEO built in: clean structure, schema, speed, meta data and a mobile version. Google indexes it well from day one. Ongoing positioning (content, links) is a separate, optional service.

items.q: Will the site work on a phone?
items.a: Yes — fully responsive and polished on phone, tablet and desktop. Most of your traffic comes from mobile anyway, so I build mobile first, not as an afterthought.

items.q: Will it really be faster than my current site?
items.a: Almost always, yes. A typical WordPress on shared hosting yields LCP of 3–5 seconds. My sites consistently sit under 1 second. It's not 'optimization' — it's a different architecture (static + edge).

items.q: Are domain and hosting included? What does it cost to run per year?
items.a: A domain runs about 70–160 PLN/year, and hosting on Vercel costs pennies or nothing. Those are the only fixed costs — no forced 'maintenance' subscription. I register both in your name, so everything is yours.

items.q: Who owns the site, code and domain once it's done?
items.a: You do, all of it. The domain and hosting are registered in your name, the source code lands in your GitHub repo, and the IP transfer is written into the contract. Nothing is rented or locked to me — another developer can take over a clean repo and carry on without a hitch.

items.q: Can I order an online store instead of a regular website?
items.a: Yes. Online store development in Warsaw is a separate service: catalog, cart, payments (Stripe, Przelewy24, BLIK), warehouse and shipping integration. Details and pricing are on the «Online stores» page.

items.q: Do you work only in Warsaw, or across Poland?
items.a: We work across all of Poland and remotely — Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław, Gdańsk, Poznań or a smaller town, it makes no difference. Calls, demos and handover happen online; the contract and payment are remote. An in-person meeting in Warsaw is available on request.

items.q: Why not build it myself on Wix or Squarespace?
items.a: If the budget is zero, a builder beats having nothing. But it has a ceiling: template looks, weak speed, capped SEO and a platform subscription forever. A builder site is rented; your own site is owned. For a business that plans to win clients from Google, a builder almost always ends up more expensive - not in money, but in lost enquiries.

items.q: Do you do redesigns? Will I lose my Google rankings?
items.a: I do, it's a frequent job. Rankings survive thanks to a proper migration: a map of old URLs, 301 redirects to the new ones, preserved heading structure and content, and an indexing check after the move. Usually rankings don't drop after migration - they grow, thanks to speed and clean markup.

items.q: How will I know the site works? What analytics do I get?
items.a: Every site ships with analytics from day one: where people come from, which pages they view, where they click, how many enquiries arrive and from which sources. Form submissions are duplicated to your Telegram or email. Once a month you open the report yourself and see the numbers - no “ask your developer for an export”.

items.q: Can I edit texts and photos myself after launch?
items.a: Yes, if you need it - I hook up a CMS: you edit copy, photos and articles in a friendly admin panel without a developer. If your content changes twice a year, a CMS is overkill: within support I apply edits faster than you'd write the brief. We pick the option that fits your team at the start.

items.q: Why is a Mini App better than a website or app?
items.a: A Mini App lives inside Telegram: the client installs nothing, needs no App Store or Google Play, and is already logged in. It opens from the bot in a second, runs at native speed and instantly knows who the user is. For booking, storefronts and payments that's less friction than a website — and a fraction of the cost of a native app.

items.q: Will the bot answer customer questions on its own, through AI?
items.a: Yes. I plug in AI that handles up to ~80% of typical questions on its own — FAQ, order status, bookings — around the clock, and passes the harder cases to a human. That's the difference between a tailor-made solution and a basic command bot.

items.q: Why hire someone when I can build a bot for free in BotFather?
items.a: A free BotFather bot handles simple commands. It won't build a Mini App with payments, CRM integrations, an admin panel, or production hosting that doesn't fall over. You get a finished, maintained business solution — not a skeleton to tinker with yourself.

items.q: Is Telegram safe for my customers' data (GDPR)?
items.a: Yes. Customer data stays on your side (your server / CRM), communication goes over Telegram's encrypted API, and data from Telegram is verified (initData). I don't store sensitive information in the chat itself — we work in line with GDPR.

items.q: How much and how long?
items.a: A simple lead bot — from €300, 1–2 weeks. A bot with AI replies and CRM integration — from €700. A Mini App with a storefront and checkout — from €1,500. Hosting is €5–30/mo, the Telegram API is free, and changes are €50/hr with no retainer. Exact quote and timeline after a short call.

items.q: How do clients pay inside Telegram?
items.a: Via Telegram Stars (the built-in currency) or crypto through TON — payment without leaving the chat. For cards and PLN I plug in Stripe or Przelewy24 inside the Mini App. We pick what fits your audience.

items.q: How popular is Telegram in Poland?
items.a: Telegram is the #2 messenger in Poland after WhatsApp — around 4 million users, and growing. For Ukrainian- and Russian-speaking audiences it's the primary channel. If your clients are on Telegram, the bot and Mini App meet them where they already are.

items.q: Can the bot connect to my CRM and site?
items.a: Yes. Leads and payments write to amoCRM, Bitrix24, HubSpot or a sheet, the bot calls your site / API, and notifications hit your Telegram. This is exactly the 'connect your tools' work — no manual data transfer.

items.q: Who owns the bot after delivery?
items.a: You do — fully. Source code, bot token, payment accounts and the database are registered to your company and handed over by contract. I don't lock you in: grow it yourself or with any developer.

items.q: Do you work only in Warsaw, or across Poland?
items.a: We work across all of Poland and remotely — Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław, Gdańsk, Poznań or a smaller town, it makes no difference. Calls, demos and handover happen online; the contract and payment are remote. An in-person meeting in Warsaw is available on request.

items.q: What does the AI audit cost and what exactly do I get?
items.a: The audit starts at €1,150 and takes five working days. You get a 12-18 page report: processes ranked by payback, a feasibility verdict for each one, a data-readiness verdict, a build quote with a fixed price and a date, and a one-page go or no-go recommendation. Plus a 90-minute live walkthrough and the recording of it.

items.q: Do I lose the fee if I go ahead with the build?
items.a: No, the whole fee is credited against the build if we sign within 60 days of the report. At €1,150 for the audit and €4,250 for the build you pay the difference. If you pick a different builder, the report is still yours and you can shop it around.

items.q: How is this different from a free call or from a pilot?
items.a: A free call gives you an opinion, the audit gives you a document with numbers, a price and a date. It is also not a pilot: in those five days I do not build a working system and I do not run a model against live data. A pilot takes weeks, costs several times more, and without an audit it usually tests the wrong process.

items.q: What if the verdict is that I should not do this yet?
items.a: A no-go verdict comes in writing, along with the conditions that would make the project worth revisiting. That outcome is normal when data is scattered or the process changes every month. The audit costs €1,150 instead of the €6,000-35,000 a full build runs to, on a system that was never going to run.

items.q: How much of my team's time does it take?

The group and regulated tier adds risk classification and the powers of KRiBSI, the Polish supervisor, which can open proceedings and impose fines from 28 October 2026. items.q: Does my chatbot have to say it is a bot?
